Panda3D](https://discourse.panda3d.org/t/how-to-add-gui-elements-into-the-window-using-pyside2-qt/27833)&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;# Panda3D Qt Embedding with QWindow and createWindowContainer&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;## Key Approaches&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;**QWidget::createWindowContainer()** is the standard Qt method for embedding QWindow-based content (including rendering windows) into Qt widget hierarchies.[3][4] This function converts a QWindow into a QWidget that can be added to regular Qt layouts.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;## Implementation Strategies&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;There are two main approaches for integrating Panda3D with Qt:&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;1. **Empty QWidget as Placeholder**: Use an empty QWidget to provide positioning and sizing information to Panda3D's own window, including parent window ID and resize parameters.[2] This approach keeps Panda3D's event loop separate.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;2. **Event Loop Integration**: Process Qt application events inside Panda3D's own event loop rather than the other way around, since Panda3D requires much more rapid event processing than typical Qt GUIs.[2]&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;## Practical Considerations&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;When embedding Panda3D in Qt, ensure the rendering window properly inherits from QWindow to be compatible with createWindowContainer().[3] The exact implementation may vary depending on whether you're using PySide2 or C++, but the fundamental pattern remains the same.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Community discussions on the Panda3D forum provide detailed examples of both approaches.[1][5] |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;/details&gt;\\\\\\\\n&lt;/tool-use&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;think&gt;&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;Thought Hack the Maze — A Python Puzzle Adventure\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA hacker-themed terminal quiz maze game. Navigate a network of cybersecurity nodes, answer Python and security questions to unlock gates, and race to reach root access.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Requirements\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Python 3.10+\\\\\\\\n- Install dependencies:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npip install -r requirements.txt\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;requirements.txt&#96; installs &#96;sqlmodel&#96; (SQLite ORM) and &#96;pytest&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Running the Game\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nOn first launch you will be prompted for a hacker handle. Progress is saved automatically to &#96;game_save.db&#96; in the current directory. Each subsequent launch resumes where you left off — including which questions you have already been asked.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Custom Maze Size\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nGenerate larger mazes with more gates using CLI flags:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --size 7 --seed 42 --gates 3\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Flag | Default | Description |\\\\\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\\\\\n| &#96;--size N&#96; | &#96;3&#96; | Width/height of the square maze (minimum 3) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;--seed N&#96; | &#96;0&#96; | Random seed for procedural generation (0 = default) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;--gates N&#96; | &#96;1&#96; | Number of puzzle gates placed along the path (minimum 1) |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen &#96;--size 3 --seed 0 --gates 1&#96; (all defaults), the hand-authored 3x3 maze is used. Any non-default value triggers procedural generation via &#96;build_square_maze&#96;. The same seed always produces the same maze layout.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFlags can be combined freely:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --size 5 --gates 2 --reset-game\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Graphical UI (PyQt6)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nLaunch the PyQt6 GUI instead of the terminal interface:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --gui\\\\\\\\npython main.py --gui --size 5 --gates 2\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRequires &#96;PyQt6&#96; to be installed. Falls back to CLI mode if unavailable.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Reset the question bank\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTo mark all questions as unasked again (e.g. start a fresh challenge with the same player record):\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --reset-game\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## How to Play\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Objective\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nYou start at the **Ingress Port** (top-left of the network grid). Reach the **Root Access Gateway** (bottom-right) to win. The default maze is 3x3, but you can generate larger grids with &#96;--size&#96;. Your score is based on elapsed time, number of moves, and hints used.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### The Map\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe maze uses **fog of war** by default. Cells you have not yet visited are hidden (&#96;###&#96;). Navigate a network of cybersecurity nodes, answer Python and security questions to unlock gates, and race to reach root access.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Requirements\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Python 3.10+\\\\\\\\n- Install dependencies:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npip install -r requirements.txt\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;requirements.txt&#96; installs &#96;sqlmodel&#96; (SQLite ORM) and &#96;pytest&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Running the Game\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nOn first launch you will be prompted for a hacker handle. Progress is saved automatically to &#96;game_save.db&#96; in the current directory. Each subsequent launch resumes where you left off — including which questions you have already been asked.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Custom Maze Size\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nGenerate larger mazes with more gates using CLI flags:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --size 7 --seed 42 --gates 3\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Flag | Default | Description |\\\\\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\\\\\n| &#96;--size N&#96; | &#96;3&#96; | Width/height of the square maze (minimum 3) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;--seed N&#96; | &#96;0&#96; | Random seed for procedural generation (0 = default) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;--gates N&#96; | &#96;1&#96; | Number of puzzle gates placed along the path (minimum 1) |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen &#96;--size 3 --seed 0 --gates 1&#96; (all defaults), the hand-authored 3x3 maze is used. Any non-default value triggers procedural generation via &#96;build_square_maze&#96;. The same seed always produces the same maze layout.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFlags can be combined freely:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --size 5 --gates 2 --reset-game\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Graphical UI (PyQt6)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nLaunch the PyQt6 GUI instead of the terminal interface:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --gui\\\\\\\\npython main.py --gui --size 5 --gates 2\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRequires &#96;PyQt6&#96; to be installed. Falls back to CLI mode if unavailable.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Reset the question bank\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTo mark all questions as unasked again (e.g. start a fresh challenge with the same player record):\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\npython main.py --reset-game\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## How to Play\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Objective\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nYou start at the **Ingress Port** (top-left of the network grid). Reach the **Root Access Gateway** (bottom-right) to win. The default maze is 3x3, but you can generate larger grids with &#96;--size&#96;. Your score is based on elapsed time, number of moves, and hints used.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### The Map\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe maze uses **fog of war** by default. [Main Loop ](https://docs.panda3d.org/1.10/python/programming/tasks-and-events/main-loop)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Running Ursina Without the Main Loop\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTo run Ursina without calling the main loop, you can use &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; instead of the blocking &#96;run()&#96; method.[5] This allows you to integrate Ursina into other event loops or frameworks.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Key Points\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Understanding the Architecture**: Ursina is built on top of Panda3D's ShowBase, and Entity objects are NodePaths.[3] This means you have access to Panda3D's underlying mechanisms.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Alternative to run()**: Instead of calling &#96;base.run()&#96; (which never returns), you can call &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; intermittently to advance the engine one frame at a time.[5] This must be called frequently enough to maintain your desired framerate.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Embedding in GUI Frameworks**: You can embed Ursina/Panda3D in external frameworks like tkinter by:\\\\\\\\n1. Initializing ShowBase with &#96;windowType='none'&#96;\\\\\\\\n2. Using &#96;WindowProperties&#96; to set a parent window and dimensions\\\\\\\\n3. Calling &#96;makeDefaultPipe()&#96; and &#96;openDefaultWindow(props=props)&#96; to render into a specific GUI component[4]\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Integration Pattern**: For frameworks with their own event loops (like wxPython or Twisted), let that framework control the main loop and call &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; periodically through its event system.[5]\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis approach is useful when you need Ursina to coexist with other Python libraries that require control of the main event loop.\\\\\\\"}],\\\\\\\"isFinal\\\\\\\":true,\\\\\\\"rejected\\\\\\\":false}\\\",\\\"toolCallBinary\\\":\\\"kgEA\\\",\\\"toolCall\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"webSearchToolCall\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"searchTerm\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Ursina engine run without main loop Panda3D ShowBase embed\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"toolCallId\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"tool_5f3f02b3-f1f6-4f3a-8510-9035d712cab\\\\\\\"},\\\\\\\"result\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"success\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"references\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"title\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Web search results for query: Ursina engine run without main loop Panda3D ShowBase embed\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"chunk\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Links:\\\\\\\\n1. Initializing ShowBase with &#96;windowType='none'&#96;\\\\\\\\n2. Using &#96;WindowProperties&#96; to set a parent window and dimensions\\\\\\\\n3. Ursina installation status\\\\n\\\\n**Ursina is not installed in this project.**\\\\n\\\\n- **&#96;requirements.txt&#96;** (&#96;/home/lhhung/504-week8/requirements.txt&#96;) lists:\\\\n  - &#96;sqlmodel&gt;=0.0.22&#96;\\\\n  - &#96;pytest&gt;=8.0&#96;\\\\n  - &#96;PyQt6&gt;=6.6&#96;\\\\n  - &#96;pytest-qt&gt;=4.4&#96;  \\\\n  No &#96;ursina&#96; or &#96;panda3d&#96; entries.\\\\n\\\\n- **No venv in the project**: No &#96;venv/&#96; or &#96;.venv/&#96; under the workspace.\\\\n\\\\n- **No &#96;ursina&#96; in site-packages**: No &#96;site-packages/ursina*&#96; under the project.\\\\n\\\\nTo add it: &#96;pip install ursina&#96; (Ursina pulls in Panda3D).\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 2. Existing integration notes in the repo\\\\n\\\\n### Plan file: &#96;/home/lhhung/.cursor/plans/ursina_gui_rollout_a5206940.plan.md&#96;\\\\n\\\\nThe plan defines a 7-phase rollout to replace the Godot 3D backend with an in-process Ursina renderer:\\\\n\\\\n| Phase | Content |\\\\n|-------|---------|\\\\n| **Phase 0** | Port GUI baseline from &#96;debug/godot-draw-harness&#96; onto &#96;ursula&#96; |\\\\n| **Phase 1** | Introduce renderer abstraction (&#96;base_backend.py&#96;, &#96;GodotBackend&#96;) |\\\\n| **Phase 2** | **In-process Ursina feasibility spike (hard gate)** — minimal embedding, lifecycle, first-frame rendering |\\\\n| **Phase 3** | Full Ursina scene, movement, facing events |\\\\n| **Phase 4** | Visual parity (facing text, 2D arrow, minimap) |\\\\n| **Phase 5** | &#96;ursina_debug_harness.py&#96; and regression coverage |\\\\n| **Phase 6** | Rollout controls (&#96;--renderer ursina|godot&#96;) and docs |\\\\n\\\\nTarget layout: &#96;MazeCanvas&#96; → &#96;UrsinaBackend&#96; → 3D scene + HUD minimap, with direction/facing events back to &#96;MazeCanvas&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;.specstory/history/2026-02-27_14-12Z-gui-availability-issue-with-pyqt6.md&#96;\\\\n\\\\nThis session includes web research on Ursina + PyQt embedding:\\\\n\\\\n- **No built-in support** for embedding Ursina in PyQt.\\\\n- **Event loop conflict**: Panda3D and Qt each have their own main loop.\\\\n- **Suggested approaches**:\\\\n  1. Multithreading (Panda3D in a separate thread via &#96;direct.stdpy.threading&#96;)\\\\n  2. Task-based: use Panda3D’s task manager and call &#96;QApplication.processEvents()&#96; each cycle\\\\n  3. Separate processes (e.g. pipes)\\\\n\\\\n- **Panda3D Qt embedding**:\\\\n  - &#96;QWidget.createWindowContainer()&#96; for QWindow-based content\\\\n  - Empty QWidget as placeholder for Panda3D window\\\\n  - Process Qt events inside Panda3D’s loop (Panda3D needs faster updates than typical Qt GUIs)\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;docs/&#96;\\\\n\\\\nNo Ursina-specific docs in &#96;docs/&#96;; only references are in &#96;.specstory&#96; and the plan.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 3. Technical risks and recommended approach\\\\n\\\\n### Panda3D + Qt embedding options\\\\n\\\\n| Approach | Notes |\\\\n|---------|------|\\\\n| **&#96;panda3d-qt&#96; / &#96;QPanda3DWidget&#96;** | &#96;panda3d-qt&#96; is not a standard Panda3D package. Third-party projects exist (e.g. &#96;ParisNeo/QPanda3D&#96;, &#96;qtpanda3d&#96; on GitLab) for PyQt5/PySide2. PyQt6 support is unclear. |\\\\n| **ShowBase window handle** | Use &#96;windowType='none'&#96; and &#96;WindowProperties&#96; to set parent window and size, then &#96;makeDefaultPipe()&#96; / &#96;openDefaultWindow(props=props)&#96; to render into a Qt widget. This is the usual low-level approach. |\\\\n\\\\n### Can Ursina run without owning the main loop?\\\\n\\\\nYes. Ursina wraps Panda3D’s &#96;ShowBase&#96;, and Panda3D supports:\\\\n\\\\n- **&#96;taskMgr.step()&#96;** instead of &#96;base.run()&#96; — advance one frame per call.\\\\n- **Embedding in external GUIs** (e.g. tkinter): init with &#96;windowType='none'&#96;, set &#96;WindowProperties&#96; for parent and size, then open the window into that widget.\\\\n- **Integration pattern**: Let Qt (or another framework) own the main loop and call &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; periodically (e.g. via &#96;QTimer&#96;).\\\\n\\\\nSo Ursina can be driven by Qt’s event loop instead of its own.\\\\n\\\\n### Main technical risks for in-process embedding\\\\n\\\\n1. **Event loop coordination**  \\\\n   Both Qt and Panda3D expect to control the main loop. You must either:\\\\n   - Drive Panda3D with &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; from Qt (e.g. via &#96;QTimer&#96;), or\\\\n   - Run Panda3D in a thread and handle cross-thread rendering carefully.\\\\n\\\\n2. **OpenGL context conflicts**  \\\\n   Qt and Panda3D both use OpenGL. Sharing or nesting contexts can cause GL errors (e.g. &#96;0x502&#96;). Multiple Panda3D views in one Qt app are especially tricky.\\\\n\\\\n3. **Platform differences**  \\\\n   X11 vs Wayland vs Windows can behave differently for embedded OpenGL windows. The plan mentions documenting “known platform limits (X11/Wayland behavior).”\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ursina’s assumptions**  \\\\n   Ursina is built around &#96;Ursina()&#96; creating and owning its window. Embedding requires:\\\\n   - Passing parent window handle via Panda3D’s &#96;WindowProperties&#96;\\\\n   - Avoiding Ursina’s default &#96;run()&#96; and using &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; instead\\\\n   - Possibly patching or subclassing Ursina’s initialization\\\\n\\\\n5. **Lifecycle and teardown**  \\\\n   Create/destroy cycles (open/close/reopen) must be robust. Phase 2’s acceptance criteria (“No crashes on open/close/reopen cycle”) target this.\\\\n\\\\n### Recommended approach (from plan and research)\\\\n\\\\n1. **Phase 2 spike as hard gate**  \\\\n   Implement a minimal &#96;UrsinaBackend&#96; that:\\\\n   - Creates/destroys the Ursina scene with the Qt widget lifecycle\\\\n   - Renders into a Qt host widget (no separate window)\\\\n   - Keeps the PyQt event loop responsive\\\\n\\\\n2. **Event loop strategy**  \\\\n   Prefer **Qt owns the loop, Panda3D steps on timer**:\\\\n   - Use a &#96;QTimer&#96; (e.g. ~16 ms for ~60 fps) to call &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96;.\\\\n   - Avoid running Panda3D’s blocking &#96;run()&#96; in the main thread.\\\\n\\\\n3. **Window embedding**  \\\\n   Use Panda3D’s &#96;WindowProperties&#96; with the Qt widget’s native window handle (&#96;winId()&#96; / &#96;WId&#96;) and &#96;createWindowContainer()&#96; if using a QWindow-based setup.\\\\n\\\\n4. **Fallback**  \\\\n   Keep the Godot backend available during migration (as in the plan) so you can fall back if the Ursina spike fails.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Summary\\\\n\\\\n| Question | Answer |\\\\n|----------|--------|\\\\n| **Ursina installed?** | No — not in &#96;requirements.txt&#96; and no venv/site-packages found. |\\\\n| **Integration notes?** | Yes — &#96;.cursor/plans/ursina_gui_rollout_a5206940.plan.md&#96; and &#96;.specstory/history/2026-02-27_14-12Z-gui-availability-issue-with-pyqt6.md&#96;. |\\\\n| **Main risks?** | Event loop coordination, OpenGL context conflicts, platform differences, Ursina’s default window ownership, lifecycle/teardown. |\\\\n| **Recommended approach?** | Phase 2 spike; Qt owns the loop and drives Panda3D via &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96; on a &#96;QTimer&#96;; embed via &#96;WindowProperties&#96; and parent window handle; keep Godot as fallback. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I have a comprehensive view of the current state and the plan. Let me review the plan critically and identify additions/clarifications needed:

1. **Phase 0 — Bootstrap GUI Baseline**: The plan says to port from `debug/godot-draw-harness` branch. The `ursula` branch currently has no `gui/` directory or `gui_main.py`. This is straightforward - cherry-pick or merge the GUI files. But the plan should clarify HOW this port happens (cherry-pick? merge? manual copy?). Also, should Godot-specific code be included or stripped?

2. **Phase 1 — Renderer Abstraction**: This is reasonable. 

For Phase 2, I need to nail down the specifics: the abstract base class interface with its methods and signals, whether `MazeCanvas` stays intact with a backend delegate or gets refactored, and how to preserve the test helper methods. The Ursina spike is the real blocker here—I should be explicit about the embedding strategy using `WindowProperties` and `winId()` with `QTimer` stepping the task manager, and what "first frame renders" actually means in practice.

On the Panda3D side, I'm weighing whether to use Ursina directly or just raw Panda3D to avoid unnecessary overhead, plus I need a fallback if the spike doesn't work out and the specific initialization pattern like `windowType='none'`. Phase 3 needs clarity on wall and floor generation from the maze snapshot, camera setup for first-person perspective, how fog-of-war translates to 3D, and gate rendering. Phase 4's minimap overlay is a bigger undertaking than it sounds—I should clarify whether that's using Panda3D's built-in 2D overlay or a separate rendering approach. Phases 5 and 6 look solid, but I'm spotting some key gaps in the overall plan.

I'm noticing we haven't addressed package installation or dependency management, the porting mechanism itself (merge versus cherry-pick versus manual), or the technical specifics of how embedding actually works. There's also the question of whether Ursina's assumptions about window ownership make raw Panda3D the better choice here. I need to think through whether Godot-specific code should even exist on the ursula branch and what to do with the `godot_maze/` directory. The acceptance criteria for Phase 2 could be tighter, and I should add a risk mitigation section around the hard gate that's missing from the plan.

The bigger issue I'm seeing now is the phase ordering itself. Phase 2 is marked as a hard gate, so if the Ursina spike fails, we stop—which means doing Phase 1 abstraction work first could be wasted effort if the spike doesn't pan out. I should either reorder these phases to validate feasibility first, or make a stronger case for why the abstraction needs to come before the spike.</details></think>

Here's my assessment of the current plan and the changes I recommend:

**Issues found in the current plan:**

1. **Phase ordering risk**: Phase 1 (refactor abstraction layer) happens before Phase 2 (Ursina feasibility spike). If the spike fails, the abstraction refactoring is wasted effort. A lightweight spike should validate embedding feasibility *first*.

2. **Phase 0 lacks specifics**: Doesn't say *how* to port (cherry-pick, merge, or manual copy). Also doesn't clarify whether Godot-specific code (`godot_maze/`, `godot_debug_harness.py`) should come along.

3. **Phase 2 lacks technical specifics**: Doesn't document the actual Panda3D embedding pattern (`windowType='none'`, `WindowProperties` with `winId()`, `QTimer` driving `taskMgr.step()`).

4. **No dependency management**: `ursina` (and transitively `panda3d`) not mentioned for `requirements.txt`.

5. **No fallback plan**: If the Ursina in-process spike fails, there's no documented alternative (e.g., subprocess model like Godot).

6. **Ursina vs raw Panda3D not addressed**: Ursina's `Ursina()` app class assumes it owns the window. For embedding, raw Panda3D's `ShowBase` with `windowType='none'` may be more appropriate. The plan should take a position.

7. **Missing: how to handle the Godot code on `ursula`**: The `ursula` branch is for Ursina - should Godot files be present at all?

8. **No explicit test strategy per phase**: Which tests gate which phases?

---

Metaclass conflict between `ABC` and `QObject`. I need to fix this -- `GodotBackend` needs QObject for signals but `BaseBackend` uses `ABC`. The solution: don't use ABC, use a regular base class. Or use QObject as the base for the backend. Let me fix `BaseBackend` to not use ABC (use regular methods with `NotImplementedError` instead) since not all backends will be QObjects.

import sys, logging

win.setCentralWidget(host)
win.show()
app.processEvents()

backend = Panda3DBackend()
backend.start(host)

    'width': 3, 'height': 3,
    'cells': [
        {'row': r, 'col': c, 'kind': 'start' if (r,c)==(0,0) else 'exit' if (r,c)==(2,2) else 'normal',

        for r in range(3) for c in range(3)
    ]
}
backend.send_maze_update(snapshot)

# Run a few frames
for _ in range(60):
    backend._step()
    app.processEvents()

print('Backend ready:', backend.is_ready())
print('Smoke test passed!')
backend.stop()
win.close()

The `--renderer panda3d` sets `use_godot = False`, but the default has `use_godot = True` with `renderer = "panda3d"`. Let me think about this...

The `use_godot` flag controls whether the Godot backend is tried by the old MazeCanvas code path. With the renderer abstraction, the `renderer` field is the primary selector. `use_godot` is kept for backward compatibility with existing test code that uses `MazeCanvas(use_godot=False)`. All phases of the Ursina Renderer Rollout Plan have been implemented. Here's a summary of what was delivered across the 7 commits on the `ursula` branch:

**Phase 0 -- GUI Baseline Port** (3 commits)
- Cherry-picked GUI baseline from `debug/godot-draw-harness`
- Brought missing `gui/` submodules (controller, forms, puzzle dialog, status bar, score board)
- Fixed `test_completion_screen_shown` visibility assertion

**Phase 1 -- Panda3D Feasibility Spike**
- Created `panda3d_embed_spike.py` proving in-process Panda3D rendering inside PyQt6
- Validated: first-frame render, 3x lifecycle cycling, responsive Qt event loop, no GL errors
- Added `panda3d>=1.10.14` to requirements.txt

**Phase 2 -- Renderer Abstraction Layer**
- Created `gui/renderers/base_backend.py` (backend interface)
- Created `gui/renderers/godot_backend.py` (extracted Godot logic)
- Refactored `MazeCanvas` to delegate 3D rendering via pluggable backends

**Phase 3 -- Panda3D Backend Implementation**
- Created `gui/renderers/panda3d_backend.py` with full 3D maze scene (floors, walls, ceilings, markers)
- First-person camera, WASD/QE keyboard input, facing events
- Updated `gui_main.py` to support `renderer='panda3d'` parameter

**Phase 4 -- Visual Parity + Minimap**
- Added in-viewport 2D minimap overlay using Panda3D aspect2d
- Grid cells, connections, player arrow indicator
- Minimap updates on movement and facing changes

**Phase 5 -- Debug Harness + Regression Coverage**
- Created `panda3d_debug_harness.py` with automated angle-sweep validation
- Added 21 backend tests (heading conversions, input handling, lifecycle, MazeCanvas integration)
- Sweep validated: 3x3 (64 actions) and 5x5 (190 actions) -- zero errors

**Phase 6 -- Rollout Controls + Documentation**
- Added `--renderer panda3d|godot` CLI flag (default: `panda3d`)
- Updated README.md with renderer docs, flag table, platform notes
- Updated interfaces.md with new signals and backend abstraction

**Final state: 158 tests passing, 9 commits ahead of origin/master.**

## Findings (by severity)

- **High — Panda3D resize handling is wired but never activated in `gui_main.py`**
  - `eventFilter` calls `_sync_panda3d_viewport()`, but `installEventFilter(self)` is only done in the `godot` branch, not `panda3d`.
  - Impact: Panda3D viewport resize updates are likely skipped; this conflicts with the phase goal of resize-safe embedding.

```176:183:gui_main.py
            if renderer == "panda3d":
                self._canvas = self._create_panda3d_canvas()
            elif renderer == "godot":
                self._viewport_host.installEventFilter(self)
                self._godot_placeholder = QLabel(
                    "Waiting for Godot viewport..."
```

```393:403:gui_main.py
    def eventFilter(self, watched: object, event: QEvent) -> bool:
        if watched is self._viewport_host and event.type() in {
            QEvent.Type.Resize,
            QEvent.Type.Show,
            QEvent.Type.WindowStateChange,
        }:
            if self._renderer == "godot":
                self._sync_embedded_godot_viewport()
            elif self._renderer == "panda3d":
                self._sync_panda3d_viewport()
```

- **Medium — Planned resize regression test is missing**
  - Phase 5 called for a resize test, but `tests/test_panda3d_backend.py` contains lifecycle + integration tests only (no resize-path assertion).
  - Impact: the resize bug above was not caught by tests.

- **Low — CLI usage help string is outdated**
  - Error usage text still omits `--renderer`, even though the parser supports it.

```648:652:main.py
    except ValueError as e:
        print(e)
        print("Usage: python main.py [--gui] [--no-godot] [--size N] [--seed N] [--gates N] [--reset-game]")
        return
```

- **Low — `--no-godot` and `--renderer` interaction is order-dependent**
  - Parser mutates both `renderer` and `use_godot`; contradictory flags can produce different results depending on argument order.

```571:584:main.py
        elif arg == "--no-godot":
            config.use_godot = False
        elif arg == "--renderer":
            ...
            config.renderer = val
            if val == "godot":
                config.use_godot = True
            else:
                config.use_godot = False
```

    b = getattr(canvas, '_backend', None)

    print('viewport size', win._viewport_host.width(), win._viewport_host.height())
    print('maze_root', bool(getattr(b, '_maze_root', None)))
    app.quit()

QTimer.singleShot(3000, probe)

---

Implemented fixes for the issues you reported.

### What I changed

- **Panda3D startup timing fixed**
  - `Panda3DBackend.start()` is now triggered lazily after the Qt viewport is shown, instead of during `MainWindow` construction.
  - This avoids early GLX/window-parent race conditions that can leave the 3D viewport black.

- **Buffered scene replay on backend start**
  - If `MazeCanvas` sends a maze snapshot before Panda3D is started, the backend now replays that snapshot immediately after startup so the scene still appears.

- **Direction/facing updates improved**
  - Added **arrow-left/arrow-right** key bindings for turning (`turn_left` / `turn_right`) in Panda3D.
  - `send_view_direction()` now also refreshes the minimap arrow immediately.

- **Resize robustness retained**
  - Viewport event filter remains installed and now works with deferred backend startup.

### Tests added/updated

- Updated `tests/test_gui_main_renderer.py` for startup/resize path.
- Updated `tests/test_panda3d_backend.py` for turn alias behavior.
- Full suite passes: **162 passed**.

- turning with `Q/E` and arrow left/right updates facing + 2D arrow

The camera parenting is fine. The real bugs are:

1. **Walls are infinitely thin** - they're `CardMaker` quads (zero-depth planes), only visible from one side. When the player is inside the maze, walls face outward and are invisible from the inside.
2. **Initial facing is "S" (H=-180)** — the default facing is South pointing away from the walls, but depending on the maze orientation, walls may be behind the camera.

Now I understand the issues clearly. Let me trace them:

1. **Walls are `CardMaker` quads with `setTwoSided(True)` but the HPR is wrong** — line 341 uses `setH(hpr[1])` but `hpr` is `(0, hpr_val, 0)`, so `hpr[1]` is the **pitch**, not heading. That means walls are oriented wrong and facing the wrong direction. Should be `node.setHpr(*hpr)`.

2. **Keyboard input doesn't reach Panda3D when embedded** — Panda3D's event system only fires when its own window has OS focus. When clicking in the PyQt window, Panda3D never gets key events. Need to forward Qt key events to Panda3D's messenger.

3. **Facing signal goes to `MazeCanvas` but `MazeCanvas` needs to forward it to the `GameController`** — let me check the canvas wiring.

Now I understand both bugs clearly. Let me write a proper test first, then fix:

**Bug 1: Wall geometry** — The `_make_wall` function uses `setH(hpr[1])` but the tuple is `(h_val, p_val, r_val)` (it's wrongly structured — the code comment says `(h, p, r)` but the values actually are `(0, h_angle, 0)` — a transposed mistake). The right fix is to use `setHpr(*hpr)`.

**Bug 2: Keyboard input** — Panda3D only receives key events when its window has focus. When embedded, focus goes to the Qt window. Need to intercept `keyPressEvent` on the `MazeCanvas` (or the parent widget) and forward to Panda3D's messenger.

**Bug 3: Facing signal** — `_on_backend_facing` calls `_set_facing_dir` but `_set_facing_dir` has a guard `if d == self._facing_dir: return` — on first call it will work, but if the same facing is emitted twice it won't update the 2D canvas. That's fine. The real issue is that facing from Panda3D's turn never gets forwarded to the `GameController`. Let me check gui_main.

The scene is all white — meaning the background color is white but the geometry still isn't rendering. This is the embedded window rendering issue. The Panda3D window is off-screen or the framebuffer isn't connected to the embedded widget. The screenshots are capturing a blank GL buffer.

The root issue is that when embedded in Qt with `setParentWindow`, Panda3D renders into the embedded sub-window but the `saveScreenshot` may be capturing a different buffer. The background didn't turn blue — so `setClearColor` is not taking effect on the current display region, OR the screenshot is capturing what's being displayed in the Qt window (the floor/ceiling color = dark navy). The scene IS rendering (we see the dark blue floor color), but the walls are invisible.

The display region DR1 has our camera attached to the player node. The scene IS rendering — the dark navy color is the floor color of the `start` cell (`(0.06, 0.2, 0.37, 1)`). What I'm seeing as "background" is actually the **floor and ceiling CardMaker geometry filling the whole view**.

The walls are there but they're the same dark color as the background. But `_WALL_COLOR = (0.25, 0.25, 0.35, 1)` should be visible against the floor. 

Wait — I need to look at the near clip: `1.0`. The cell walls are only 2 units away from the player (`CELL_SIZE/2 = 2.0`). The near clip of `1.0` should allow rendering at 2 units. But the wall is a flat quad AT the position. If the camera near clip is 1.0 and the wall is exactly at `y=-4` while the player is at `y=-2`, the wall is 2 units away — that should be fine.

The real issue is the **wall geometry orientation**. Let me think again: the `_make_wall` function applies only `setH(hpr[1])` instead of `setHpr(*hpr)`. For North wall `hpr=(0,0,0)` so `hpr[1]=0` (pitch=0), setting `setH(0)` which means heading=0. But the card's default faces +Y — the NORTH wall (at y=0) should face into the cell (-Y direction), so it needs H=180 to face south (into the cell). With `setTwoSided(True)` it doesn't matter — BUT wait, is there a transparency/depth issue?

Wait — after `q` (turn left), facing went from S→E? That's wrong. S→turn_left should be S→E in our compass mapping? Let me verify: facing S (H=180), turn_left means turn_left which is `(H - 90) % 360 = 90 = E`. Actually turning LEFT while facing South should give you East? In a compass: S - 90° = E (counterclockwise). But from a first-person perspective, turn_left while facing South should give you East (to your right is West, to your left is East). Actually this depends on convention:

In Panda3D: H increases counterclockwise (left turn). `S=180`, turn_left = H - 90 = 90 = E. But if you're facing South and turn left (your left), you now face East. Is East to your left when facing South? No — if you're facing South, left is East, right is West. So turning LEFT gives East. That is correct!

Now the key forwarding works via messenger. The fix is to override `keyPressEvent`/`keyReleaseEvent` in `MazeCanvas` to forward to the backend.

I see that for panda3d, `_canvas` is the `MazeCanvas` with the backend, and it's placed in the splitter BELOW `_viewport_host`. But `_viewport_host` is where Panda3D actually renders! The `MazeCanvas` itself just shows the 2D map below.

The problem with keyboard focus is: the 3D viewport is the `_viewport_host`, but key events need to go to `MazeCanvas` which is a separate widget below. `MazeCanvas.keyPressEvent` will only fire if the user clicks on the 2D canvas widget, not the 3D viewport above.

The fix: also install a key event filter on `_viewport_host` (or the main window) that forwards keys to the canvas. Let me check how the `_viewport_host` is structured for panda3d:

For `panda3d`: `_viewport_host` has a layout, and Panda3D renders INTO `_viewport_host`'s native window. The canvas (MazeCanvas) is separate. We need to intercept key events on the main window and forward to the canvas.

The cleanest solution is to override `keyPressEvent` on `MainWindow` to forward to the canvas:

All clean. Here's a summary of all the fixes made:

---

**Root cause analysis and fixes:**

**1. Walls were invisible** — The wall color `(0.25, 0.25, 0.35)` was too close to the dark ceiling/floor colors in the dim ambient lighting. Fixed by:
- Brightening wall color to `(0.55, 0.55, 0.70)` — now clearly visible as blue-grey panels
- Increasing ambient light from `0.35` to `0.6` and adding a back fill light
- Setting a dark background clear color `(0.06, 0.05, 0.10)` matching the maze atmosphere
- Setting FOV from `39°` to `75°` — the default Panda3D FOV was extremely narrow (nearly telephoto)

**2. Facing/keyboard input not working** — When Panda3D is embedded inside a Qt widget, it doesn't receive OS keyboard focus. Fixed by:
- Added `inject_key(panda_key, pressed)` to `BaseBackend` and `Panda3DBackend` — forwards via `messenger.send()`
- Added `keyPressEvent`/`keyReleaseEvent` to `MazeCanvas` to call `inject_key` with the Qt→Panda3D key name mapping
- Added `keyPressEvent`/`keyReleaseEvent` to `MainWindow` to route keys to canvas when renderer is `panda3d`
- Added `setFocusPolicy(StrongFocus)` to `MazeCanvas` so it accepts keyboard focus

**3. GLXBadDrawable on quit** — Fixed by explicitly deactivating the Panda3D window and calling `graphicsEngine.removeWindow()` before `destroy()` in `stop()`.

Found the bug. `_ensure_panda3d_started` calls `backend.start()` **every time** the `eventFilter` fires (Resize, Show, WindowStateChange) — but `backend.start()` has a guard `if self._started: return`. So after the first `start()`, subsequent resize events call `_sync_panda3d_viewport` → `_handle_resize()` which resizes the Panda3D window to `_viewport_host.width/height`. That should work.

The real issue is **when `start()` is first called**, the widget might not be fully sized yet. The `showEvent` on `MainWindow` fires before the layout engine has completed the first pass. Let me add logging to trace the actual sizes:

The process hung without producing any output — likely blocked on the Panda3D `openDefaultWindow` call. The trace script never got to print. Let me use a simpler approach — add temporary logging directly to `_ensure_panda3d_started` and `_handle_resize` and just read what the actual problem is from first principles:

The key insight from the earlier test: when the host is 882×428, Panda3D fills it perfectly. In the real app the viewport is only filling "70% of the window." The number `~70%` of the left panel width (~400px) is roughly 280px — that's `640*0.44` suggesting Panda3D initialized at `640×480` (its hardcoded default) and never resized to match the final widget.

The problem: `_ensure_panda3d_started` calls `backend.start(viewport_host)` which captures the widget size at that instant. `_handle_resize` is called right after but `start()` has a guard that returns early if already started — except `start()` creates the window with whatever size the widget has at that moment. If `showEvent` fires before layout completes, the widget might be 640×480 or similar.

The fix: **always call `_handle_resize` after a short delay once the window is shown**, not just immediately after `start()`. Use a `QTimer.singleShot` to let the layout settle:

Now address the **texture** issue. The user sees "very basic filled shapes" — that's because `CardMaker` produces flat geometry with no UV mapping, and `setColor()` overrides any texture. The walls need procedural textures. Let me add a simple brick/stone texture using Panda3D's `Texture` API — we can generate a procedural texture in numpy or via `PixelBuffer`:

# Test procedural texture generation in Panda3D
import sys
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget
from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt
from gui.renderers.panda3d_backend import Panda3DBackend

app = QApplication(sys.argv)
host = QWidget()
host.setAttribute(Qt.WidgetAttribute.WA_NativeWindow, True)
host.setMinimumSize(640, 480)
host.show()
app.processEvents()

b = Panda3DBackend()
b.start(host)

from panda3d.core import Texture, PNMImage, CardMaker, LVector4, TextureStage

# Build a 64x64 brick pattern procedurally
def make_brick_texture(base_r=0.45, base_g=0.40, base_b=0.52, brick_r=0.30, brick_g=0.27, brick_b=0.38, size=64):
    img = PNMImage(size, size)
    img.addAlpha()
    bw, bh = size // 4, size // 8  # brick width, height
    mortar = 2  # mortar thickness in pixels
    for y in range(size):
        row = y // bh
        offset = (bw // 2) * (row % 2)
        for x in range(size):
            bx = (x + offset) % size
            in_mortar_x = (bx % bw) < mortar
            in_mortar_y = (y % bh) < mortar
            if in_mortar_x or in_mortar_y:
                # mortar: slightly lighter/neutral
                img.setXel(x, y, base_r * 1.1, base_g * 1.1, base_b * 1.1)
            else:
                # brick face with slight variation
                noise = ((x * 7 + y * 13) % 17) / 17.0 * 0.08 - 0.04
                img.setXel(x, y, brick_r + noise, brick_g + noise, brick_b + noise)
            img.setAlpha(x, y, 1.0)
    tex = Texture()
    tex.load(img)
    tex.setWrapU(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setWrapV(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setMagfilter(Texture.FT_linear)
    tex.setMinfilter(Texture.FT_linear_mipmap_linear)
    return tex

wall_tex = make_brick_texture()
print("texture created:", wall_tex.getXSize(), wall_tex.getYSize())

# Apply to a test card
root = b._base.render.attachNewNode("test")
cm = CardMaker("test_wall")
cm.setFrame(-2, 2, 0, 3)
cm.setUvRange((0,0), (2, 1.5))  # tile the texture 2x in U, 1.5x in V
card = root.attachNewNode(cm.generate())
card.setPos(0, 3, 0)
card.setH(180)
card.setTexture(wall_tex)

b._base.cam.reparentTo(b._base.render)

b._base.camLens.setFov(90)

b._base.win.saveScreenshot("test_texture.png")
for _ in range(3): b._step(); app.processEvents()

    mortar = max(2, size // 40)
    for y in range(size):
        row = y // bh
        offset = (bw // 2) * (row % 2)
        for x in range(size):
            bx = (x + offset) % size

    tex.setWrapU(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setWrapV(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setMagfilter(Texture.FT_linear)
    tex.setMinfilter(Texture.FT_linear_mipmap_linear)
    return tex

def make_floor_texture(size=128):
    img = PNMImage(size, size)
    tile = size // 4
    grout = max(2, size // 32)
    for y in range(size):
        for x in range(size):
            if (x % tile) < grout or (y % tile) < grout:
                img.setXelA(x, y, 0.07, 0.10, 0.18, 1.0)
            else:

                img.setXelA(x, y, 0.10 + noise, 0.15 + noise, 0.27 + noise, 1.0)
    tex = Texture()
    tex.load(img)
    tex.setWrapU(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setWrapV(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setMagfilter(Texture.FT_linear)
    tex.setMinfilter(Texture.FT_linear_mipmap_linear)
    return tex

    for y in range(size):
        for x in range(size):
            if (x % tile) < grout or (y % tile) < grout:
                img.setXelA(x, y, 0.07, 0.10, 0.18, 1.0)
            else:
                noise = (((x * 5 + y * 11) ^ y) % 23) / 23.0 * 0.06
                img.setXelA(x, y, 0.10 + noise, 0.15 + noise, 0.27 + noise, 1.0)
    tex = Texture()
    tex.load(img)
    tex.setWrapU(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setWrapV(Texture.WM_repeat)
    tex.setMagfilter(Texture.FT_linear)
    tex.setMinfilter(Texture.FT_linear_mipmap_linear)
    return tex

wall_tex = make_brick_texture()
floor_tex = make_floor_texture()
print("Textures created")

root = b._base.render.attachNewNode("test")
b._base.win.setClearColor((0.06, 0.05, 0.10, 1))

# Wall ahead
cm = CardMaker("wall")
cm.setFrame(-2, 2, 0, 3)
cm.setUvRange(Point2(0, 0), Point2(2, 1.5))
card = root.attachNewNode(cm.generate())
card.setPos(0, 4, 0); card.setH(180); card.setTwoSided(True)
card.setTexture(wall_tex)

# Left wall
cm2 = CardMaker("lwall")
cm2.setFrame(-4, 0, 0, 3)
cm2.setUvRange(Point2(0, 0), Point2(2, 1.5))
lcard = root.attachNewNode(cm2.generate())
lcard.setPos(-2, 0, 0); lcard.setH(90); lcard.setTwoSided(True)
lcard.setTexture(wall_tex)

# Floor
cmf = CardMaker("floor")
cmf.setFrame(-4, 4, -4, 4)
cmf.setUvRange(Point2(0, 0), Point2(2, 2))
floor = root.attachNewNode(cmf.generate())
floor.setPos(0, 0, 0); floor.setP(-90); floor.setTwoSided(True)
floor.setTexture(floor_tex)

b._base.cam.reparentTo(b._base.render)
b._base.cam.setPos(0, 0, 1.6)
b._base.cam.setHpr(0, 0, 0)
b._base.camLens.setFov(90)

for _ in range(15): b._step(); app.processEvents()
b._base.win.saveScreenshot("test_tex3.png")
for _ in range(3): b._step(); app.processEvents()
import os; print("Tex3:", os.path.getsize("test_tex3.png"), "bytes")
b.stop()
app.quit()

CardMaker does generate normals. The problem is that:
1. The walls at the far end of a corridor are 4-8 units away from the player
2. With `attenuation=(0.5, 0, 0.003)`: at 4 units → factor = 1/(0.5 + 0 + 0.003×16) = 1/0.548 ≈ 1.82 (>1, capped to 1, actually fine). At 8 units → 1/(0.5 + 0.192) = 1.44 (still fine). 

Wait, the attenuation actually should work. The issue must be that the wall normals point AWAY from the player (flat cards face outward), and with `setTwoSided(True)`, Panda3D renders both faces but normals are still pointing outward — so point light calculations give 0 for the inward-facing surface.

The fix: either flip the card normals, or use `setLightOff` and then `setLightOn` with proper normal-flipping, or simply apply the point light as two-sided shading. The quickest fix is to **not use `setTwoSided` and instead correctly orient each card to face inward**:

The wall orientation should be: the card's front face points INTO the corridor (toward the player). Currently walls are placed at the cell boundary and `setH` rotates them. Let me reconsider:

- North wall at `(cx, cy+half, 0)` with `H=0`: card faces +Y = facing away from cell (outward). Should be `H=180` to face inward (-Y).
- South wall at `(cx, cy-half, 0)` with `H=180`: card faces -Y = facing away from cell. Should be `H=0`.
- East wall at `(cx+half, cy, 0)` with `H=-90`: card faces -X = away. Should be `H=90`.
- West wall at `(cx-half, cy, 0)` with `H=90`: card faces +X = away. Should be `H=-90`.

The fix is to flip all wall headings 180°, remove `setTwoSided`, and then point light normals will face into the corridor correctly:

Let me reconsider. Player at `(0,0)` = world `(2,-2)`, facing S (`H=180` = looking in `-Y` direction). The corridor goes South:
- The wall at `(cx+half=4, cy=-2, 0)` with new `H=90` (East wall of start cell). Card with `H=90` faces `+X` (east). But the INSIDE of this wall should face `W` (-X), toward the player in the corridor. So `H=90` is wrong — it should face left wall = face into corridor = face `-X` = `H=270` or `H=-90`.

I have the logic backwards again. Let me be systematic:

- **East wall** (right side of corridor): located at `x=cx+half` (east edge). Player in the cell sees this wall to their right. The wall normal should point **westward** (-X) to face the player. CardMaker normal default is +Y. `setH(-90)` = rotate -90° = card faces `-X`. So East wall should use `H=-90`.
- **West wall**: located at `x=cx-half`. Normal should point `+X`. `setH(90)` = faces `+X`. Correct.
- **North wall**: at `y=cy+half`. Normal should point `-Y` (south, into cell). `setH(180)`. Correct.
- **South wall**: at `y=cy-half`. Normal should point `+Y` (north, into cell). `setH(0)`. Correct.

My new specs were: `N→H=180, S→H=0, E→H=90, W→H=-90`. But East should be `H=-90` and West `H=90`. I have E and W swapped!

All 4 walls have normal `(0, -1, 0)` — pointing in `-Y` direction. That's the **default** CardMaker normal before rotation. The `setH()` call rotates the node but Panda3D doesn't update the stored vertex normals — it applies the transform at render time. So ALL normals read as `(0,-1,0)` in local space, but in world space they should be different after the transform.

The issue is the `GeomVertexReader` reads in **local** space. In world space the normals ARE rotated. Let me verify by getting the normal in world space:

The key insight: CardMaker's default face is +Y (H=0). For the West wall (`H=90`): in world space the face is +X direction. The player point light is at `(2, -2, 1.6)` and the West wall is at `x=0`, so the light-to-surface vector is `(-2, 0, ...)` pointing in `-X` direction. The wall normal faces `+X`. Dot product is **-1** (opposite). The wall is **facing away from the light source** when the point light is inside the cell!

That's exactly the problem. The walls face INTO the cell but the point light is AT the camera inside the cell. For the west wall at x=0: its normal points `+X` (east, into the cell). The light is at x=2 (also inside the cell). The vector from wall to light = `+X` = same direction as normal. Dot product = **+1** — **this should be fully lit!**

The west wall is completely invisible even with strong ambient light! The wall at `x=0, y=-2` with camera at `(2,-2,1.6)` facing south (H=180). The wall is to the LEFT of the camera. With FOV=75°, the west wall should be visible at ~45° to the left. But it's invisible.

The issue is the **camera is facing south (H=180) and the west wall at x=0 is only 2 units to the left**. With 75° FOV (±37.5° horizontal), the wall at angle ≈ `atan2(2, 0)` from forward direction... wait, the wall extends from y=-4 to y=0. The camera is at y=-2, looking in -Y. So the wall spans from `y=-4` to `y=0` at `x=0`. The closest point is `(0, -2)` which is directly to the left (west) of the camera. The wall should fill the left side of the frame.

Actually I bet the card is **inside the wall** — the card is at `x=0` but extends in the Y direction, and the camera is looking south (-Y). The card's extent from the face (+X direction from `setH(90)`) should be visible from the right side... but with H=180 looking south, the left side has x<2. The west wall at x=0 should be to the LEFT.

Let me try placing the camera looking TOWARD the west wall (H=270 = facing west = -X):

The real issue might be simply that `CardMaker` with `setFrame(-2,2,0,3)` has its card centered at the origin in local XZ. When we do `setH(90)` and `setPos(0,-2,0)`, the card is rotated so it spans from y=-4 to y=0 at x=0. Camera at (2,-2,1.6) facing -Y doesn't see this because the wall is at x=0 which is to the LEFT and with H=180 (facing south) the left edge of the frustum is about x=2-dist*tan(37.5°). At 2 units, that's x=2-2*0.77=0.46. The wall at x=0 is just OUTSIDE the left frustum edge!

**The wall is just outside the horizontal FOV.** At 75° FOV total (±37.5°), from position (2,-2) looking south (-Y), the leftmost visible X at Y=-2 (same Y as camera) is `x = 2 - 0 * tan(37.5°) = 2`. At Y=-4 (2 units ahead), leftmost X = `2 - 2*tan(37.5°) = 2 - 1.54 = 0.46`. The wall at x=0 is just outside the 0.46 boundary. The wall only becomes visible when you look left!

This is correct behavior. The camera is in the corner cell and looking south. The west wall is slightly to the left and outside the FOV. That's geometrically accurate. The issue I was seeing was correct — the walls ARE rendering when they're in view, just the scene happened to be a corner case.

Here's a summary of all the fixes made:

---

**1. Viewport fill (layout fix)**
`showEvent` now defers `_ensure_panda3d_started` by one event-loop tick (`QTimer.singleShot(0, ...)`) so Qt's layout engine assigns final sizes before Panda3D reads `viewport_host.width/height`. After `start()`, four staggered resize syncs (50ms, 150ms, 300ms, 600ms) ensure the Panda3D window catches up to the final laid-out size.

**2. Textures — brick walls, tiled floor, stone ceiling**
Added three procedural texture generators (`_make_brick_texture`, `_make_floor_texture`, `_make_ceiling_texture`) that build `PNMImage` bitmaps in Python with brick mortar patterns and tile grout lines. Textures are generated once via `_setup_textures()` after Panda3D starts and cached. Applied via `setTexture()` + `setColorScale()` so colors tint rather than override. UV ranges set via `CardMaker.setUvRange()`.

**3. Correct wall normals for lighting**
All four wall orientations were fixed so card normals face INTO the corridor (toward the player). CardMaker default normal is `+Y`; the correct headings are N→H=180, S→H=0, E→H=270 (−90), W→H=90. Removed `setTwoSided(True)` so point-light diffuse calculations use the correct inward-facing normals.

**4. Player torch lighting**
Replaced four directional lights with a low ambient + a `PointLight` attached to the camera node, simulating a torch/lantern. The quadratic attenuation `(0.3, 0.0, 0.003)` with color `(2.5, 2.4, 2.2)` gives warm light on nearby walls with natural falloff into darkness for distant areas.

**5. Test fix**
`_FakeBackend` in `test_gui_main_renderer.py` gained `is_ready()` to match the new `_ensure_panda3d_started` guard.

# Patch _ensure_panda3d_started to print sizes, then quit after 2s
import sys, os
os.environ["DISPLAY"] = os.environ.get("DISPLAY", ":0")

from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication
from PyQt6.QtCore import QTimer
app = QApplication(sys.argv)

import gui_main as gm

sizes_log = []

orig_start = None

def patched_ensure(self):
    if self._viewport_host and hasattr(self._canvas, '_backend') and self._canvas._backend:
        b = self._canvas._backend
        w = self._viewport_host.width()
        h = self._viewport_host.height()
        started = b._started
        sizes_log.append(f"ensure: host={w}x{h} already_started={started}")
    from gui.renderers.panda3d_backend import Panda3DBackend
    # Wrap start() to log the size it captures
    orig_bstart = Panda3DBackend.start
    def logged_start(self2, parent_widget):
        sizes_log.append(f"  backend.start() host_size={parent_widget.width()}x{parent_widget.height()}")
        orig_bstart(self2, parent_widget)
        if self2._base and self2._base.win:
            sizes_log.append(f"  panda_win after start={self2._base.win.getXSize()}x{self2._base.win.getYSize()}")
    Panda3DBackend.start = logged_start

    orig_ensure(self)
    Panda3DBackend.start = orig_bstart

    if self._viewport_host and hasattr(self._canvas, '_backend') and self._canvas._backend:
        b = self._canvas._backend
        if b._base and b._base.win:
            sizes_log.append(f"  panda_win after ensure={b._base.win.getXSize()}x{b._base.win.getYSize()}")

orig_ensure = gm.MainWindow._ensure_panda3d_started
gm.MainWindow._ensure_panda3d_started = patched_ensure

orig_sync = gm.MainWindow._sync_panda3d_viewport
def patched_sync(self):
    if self._viewport_host and hasattr(self._canvas, '_backend') and self._canvas._backend:
        b = self._canvas._backend
        win_sz = f"{b._base.win.getXSize()}x{b._base.win.getYSize()}" if (b._base and b._base.win) else "no_win"
        sizes_log.append(f"sync: host={self._viewport_host.width()}x{self._viewport_host.height()} panda={win_sz}")
    orig_sync(self)
gm.MainWindow._sync_panda3d_viewport = patched_sync

from main import StartupConfig
config = StartupConfig(gui=True, renderer='panda3d', maze_size=3, maze_seed=42)

def quit_and_print():
    for line in sizes_log:
        print(line)
    app.quit()

QTimer.singleShot(2000, quit_and_print)
gm.gui_main(config)

    snapshot = {'width':3,'height':3,'cells':[
        {'row':r,'col':c,'kind':'start' if(r,c)==(0,0) else 'exit' if(r,c)==(2,2) else 'normal',
         'visible':True,'is_player':(r,c)==(0,0),'has_gate':False,'solved':False,
         'connections':['E','S'] if(r,c)==(0,0) else ['N','W'] if(r,c)==(2,2) else ['N','S','E','W']}
        for r in range(3) for c in range(3)]}
    canvas.update_maze(type('MS', (), {'width':3,'height':3,'cells':[type('CV',(),{'row':c['row'],'col':c['col'],'kind':c['kind'],'visible':c['visible'],'is_player':c['is_player'],'has_gate':c['has_gate'],'solved':c['solved'],'connections':c['connections']})() for c in snapshot['cells']]})())

def check_50():
    print(f"T=50ms viewport_host: {viewport_host.width()}x{viewport_host.height()}")
    backend._handle_resize()
    print(f"T=50ms panda_win after resize: {backend._base.win.getXSize()}x{backend._base.win.getYSize()}")

def check_300():
    print(f"T=300ms viewport_host: {viewport_host.width()}x{viewport_host.height()}")
    backend._handle_resize()
    print(f"T=300ms panda_win after resize: {backend._base.win.getXSize()}x{backend._base.win.getYSize()}")

def check_600():
    print(f"T=600ms viewport_host: {viewport_host.width()}x{viewport_host.height()}")
    backend._handle_resize()
    print(f"T=600ms panda_win after resize: {backend._base.win.getXSize()}x{backend._base.win.getYSize()}")
    for _ in range(10): backend._step(); app.processEvents()
    backend._base.win.saveScreenshot("test_layout_final.png")
    import os; print(f"screenshot: {os.path.getsize('test_layout_final.png')} bytes")
    backend.stop()
    app.quit()

QTimer.singleShot(0, do_start)
QTimer.singleShot(50, check_50)
QTimer.singleShot(300, check_300)
QTimer.singleShot(600, check_600)
app.exec()

---

The Panda3D window IS filling 390×408 — that screenshot shows it filling the full widget. So in isolation the layout works. The problem in the real app must be the **right panel (`right` widget with `setMinimumWidth(300)`) is consuming more space than expected**, leaving the left panel narrow.

But the user says the 3D view doesn't fill the viewport widget itself — meaning the Panda3D subwindow is smaller than `_viewport_host`. The key clue from the trace: **at T=600ms, `viewport_host=390x408` but `panda_win` only updates to 390×408 after the resize.** At T=50ms panda was still 390×404.

The issue is the `_handle_resize` is calling `requestProperties` but it's **asynchronous** — Panda3D processes property changes on the next render frame, not immediately. The staggered timers help but there's a race. The real fix is to **drive a few `taskMgr.step()` calls after requesting the resize** to flush the property change.

Let me check `_handle_resize`:

---

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="read_file_v2">
<details><summary>Tool use: **read_file_v2** • Read file: /home/lhhung/504-week8/gui/renderers/panda3d_backend.py</summary>

</details>
</tool-use>

---

The fix: after `requestProperties`, immediately call `taskMgr.step()` a few times to flush the resize:

---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="edit_file_v2">

<details><summary>Tool use: **edit_file_v2** • Edit file: /home/lhhung/504-week8/gui/renderers/panda3d_backend.py</summary>

</details>

</tool-use>

---

Also, in `_sync_panda3d_viewport`, call `_handle_resize` directly (it already does). But the issue is that `eventFilter` fires on `Resize` events for `_viewport_host` — that should also trigger `_handle_resize`. Let me check if resize events are actually being delivered:

---

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="read_file_v2">
<details><summary>Tool use: **read_file_v2** • Read file: /home/lhhung/504-week8/gui_main.py</summary>

</details>
</tool-use>

---

The `eventFilter` calls `_ensure_panda3d_started()` then `_sync_panda3d_viewport()` on every resize of `_viewport_host`. But `_ensure_panda3d_started` now has a guard: if already started, it calls `_handle_resize` immediately. Let me re-read what it does now:

---

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="read_file_v2">
<details><summary>Tool use: **read_file_v2** • Read file: /home/lhhung/504-week8/gui_main.py</summary>

</details>
</tool-use>

---

Good. The `eventFilter` calls `_sync_panda3d_viewport` which calls `_handle_resize`. With the new `_handle_resize` that flushes via `step()`, resize events should now fully apply immediately.

But there's still the initial startup issue — the **first** `_ensure_panda3d_started` fires from `showEvent` → `QTimer.singleShot(0, ...)`. At that point the viewport may still be at provisional size. The staggered timers at 50/150/300/600ms should catch the final size.

Actually, there's a better approach. Instead of staggered timers, use a `QTimer` that repeatedly checks until the Panda3D window matches the host size:

    if (win_w == host_w and win_h == host_h) or attempts[0] >= 8:
        finish()
    else:
        delay = min(50 * (2 ** attempts[0]), 400)
        QTimer.singleShot(delay, poll)

def finish():
    for _ in range(10): backend._step(); app.processEvents()
    backend._base.win.saveScreenshot("test_poll.png")
    import os; print("screenshot:", os.path.getsize("test_poll.png"), "bytes")
    backend.stop()
    app.quit()

QTimer.singleShot(0, do_start)
app.exec()

All 162 tests pass. Here's what was done:

**Root cause:** `requestProperties(props)` in Panda3D is asynchronous — it queues a resize request but doesn't apply it until the next `taskMgr.step()` call. So `_handle_resize()` was firing but the size change wasn't actually taking effect.

**Fix 1 — `_handle_resize` now flushes immediately:**
After calling `requestProperties`, it runs 3 `taskMgr.step()` calls inline so the resize is processed before returning. It also skips the resize if the size already matches, avoiding unnecessary work.

**Fix 2 — Polling size-sync at startup:**
`_ensure_panda3d_started` now calls `_schedule_panda3d_size_sync()` after `backend.start()`. This uses exponential back-off polling (50ms → 100ms → 200ms → 400ms, up to 8 attempts ≈ 2.5 seconds) — it keeps calling `_handle_resize()` until `panda_win.getXSize() == viewport_host.width()`. This handles the race between Panda3D initialization and Qt's layout engine finishing its first pass.

import os, sys

from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget
from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QGuiApplication

app = QApplication(sys.argv)
host = QWidget()
host.setAttribute(Qt.WidgetAttribute.WA_NativeWindow, True)
host.resize(800, 500)
host.show()
app.processEvents()

print('host logical:', host.width(), host.height())

b.stop()
app.quit()
PY

### What was happening
This is a **HiDPI / fractional-scaling mismatch**: Qt reports widget sizes in **device-independent pixels**, but Panda3D sizes embedded windows in **physical pixels**. So Panda3D’s child window ended up smaller and “stuck” in a corner of the viewport; resizing didn’t help because it kept using the wrong units.

### What I changed
- **`gui/renderers/panda3d_backend.py`**: Panda3D now uses `widget.devicePixelRatioF()` to size/rescale the embedded window in **physical pixels** (both on `start()` and `_handle_resize()`).
- **`gui_main.py`**: the startup “size sync” compares against **physical pixel** sizes too.

### Try again
Run:

```bash
python main.py --gui --renderer panda3d
```

If it *still* doesn’t fill the viewport, paste the single log line that starts with **`Panda3D backend started (logical=... px=... dpr=...)`** (it will tell us what Qt’s DPR is on your setup).

+def _make_floor_texture(size: int = 128):

+    from panda3d.core import PNMImage, Texture

+    tile = size // 4
+    grout = max(2, size // 32)
+    for y in range(size):

+    tex.setWrapV(Texture.WM_repeat)
+    tex.setMagfilter(Texture.FT_linear)
+    tex.setMinfilter(Texture.FT_linear_mipmap_linear)
+    return tex
+
+

+    def _ensure_panda3d_started(self) -&gt; None:
+        """Start Panda3D backend lazily once the viewport host is shown."""
+        if self._renderer != "panda3d":
+            return
+        if not isinstance(self._canvas, MazeCanvas):
+            return
+        if self._viewport_host is None:
+            return
+        backend = self._canvas._backend
+        if backend is None:
+            return
+        if not backend.is_ready():
+            # Starting too early (before native show/map) can trigger GLX drawable errors.
+            backend.start(self._viewport_host)
+            # The Qt layout engine may not have assigned final sizes yet.
+            # Poll until the Panda3D window matches the host widget, giving up after ~1s.
+            self._schedule_panda3d_size_sync()
+        elif hasattr(backend, "_handle_resize"):
+            backend._handle_resize()
+
+    def _schedule_panda3d_size_sync(self, _attempts: int = 0) -&gt; None:
+        """Poll until the Panda3D window matches the host widget size, then stop.
+
+        The Qt layout engine finalises child-widget sizes asynchronously after
+        &#96;&#96;show()&#96;&#96;.  We retry with exponential back-off for up to ~1 second so
+        the Panda3D sub-window always fills its host.
+        """
+        if self._viewport_host is None or not isinstance(self._canvas, MazeCanvas):
+            return
+        backend = self._canvas._backend
+        if backend is None or not backend.is_ready():
+            return
+        backend._handle_resize()
+
+        # Compare in physical pixels (Qt uses device-independent pixels).
+        try:
+            dpr = float(self._viewport_host.devicePixelRatioF())
+        except Exception:
+            dpr = 1.0
+        host_px_w = max(1, int(round(self._viewport_host.width() * dpr)))
+        host_px_h = max(1, int(round(self._viewport_host.height() * dpr)))
+
+        base = getattr(backend, "_base", None)
+        win = base.win if base is not None else None
+        if win is None:
+            return
+        already_correct = win.getXSize() == host_px_w and win.getYSize() == host_px_h
+
+        if already_correct or _attempts &gt;= 8:
+            return
+        delay_ms = min(50 * (2 ** _attempts), 400)
+        QTimer.singleShot(
+            delay_ms,
+            lambda: self._schedule_panda3d_size_sync(_attempts + 1),
+        )

is\\\":[],\\\"conversationState\\\":{\\\"rootPromptMessagesJson\\\":[],\\\"turnsOld\\\":[],\\\"todos\\\":[],\\\"pendingToolCalls\\\":[],\\\"turns\\\":[],\\\"previousWorkspaceUris\\\":[],\\\"fileStates\\\":{},\\\"summaryArchives\\\":[],\\\"turnTimings\\\":[],\\\"fileStatesV2\\\":{},\\\"subagentStates\\\":{},\\\"selfSummaryCount\\\":0,\\\"readPaths\\\":[]},\\\"text\\\":\\\"\\\\nHere’s a summary of the renderer backend architecture:\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Renderer Backend Architecture Summary\\\\n\\\\n## 1. BaseBackend Interface (&#96;gui/renderers/base_backend.py&#96;)\\\\n\\\\n&#96;BaseBackend&#96; defines the interface for 3D renderer backends. It is not an ABC to avoid metaclass conflicts with QObject subclasses.\\\\n\\\\n### Lifecycle methods\\\\n\\\\n| Method | Signature | Purpose |\\\\n|--------|-----------|---------|\\\\n| &#96;start&#96; | &#96;(parent_widget: QWidget) -&gt; None&#96; | Initialize rendering into the parent widget |\\\\n| &#96;stop&#96; | &#96;() -&gt; None&#96; | Tear down rendering resources |\\\\n| &#96;is_ready&#96; | &#96;() -&gt; bool&#96; | Return &#96;True&#96; when the backend is initialized and ready for data |\\\\n\\\\n### Data input methods\\\\n\\\\n| Method | Signature | Purpose |\\\\n|--------|-----------|---------|\\\\n| &#96;send_maze_update&#96; | &#96;(snapshot_dict: dict) -&gt; None&#96; | Push a full maze snapshot (plain dict) to the renderer |\\\\n| &#96;send_highlight_player&#96; | &#96;(row: int, col: int) -&gt; None&#96; | Update the player highlight position |\\\\n| &#96;send_view_direction&#96; | &#96;(direction: str) -&gt; None&#96; | Set camera/view facing direction (N/S/E/W) |\\\\n\\\\n### Input injection (for embedded backends)\\\\n\\\\n| Method | Signature | Purpose |\\\\n|--------|-----------|---------|\\\\n| &#96;inject_key&#96; | &#96;(panda_key: str, *, pressed: bool) -&gt; None&#96; | Inject key press/release by name (e.g. &#96;'w'&#96;, &#96;'arrow_left'&#96;). Default is no-op; Panda3DBackend overrides. |\\\\n\\\\n### Event callbacks\\\\n\\\\n| Method | Signature | Purpose |\\\\n|--------|-----------|---------|\\\\n| &#96;on_direction&#96; | &#96;(callback: Callable[[str], None]) -&gt; None&#96; | Register callback for movement direction events |\\\\n| &#96;on_facing&#96; | &#96;(callback: Callable[[str], None]) -&gt; None&#96; | Register callback for facing-change events |\\\\n\\\\n### Internal helpers\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;_emit_direction(direction: str)&#96; — invokes &#96;_on_direction_cb&#96; if direction is N/S/E/W\\\\n- &#96;_emit_facing(direction: str)&#96; — invokes &#96;_on_facing_cb&#96; if direction is N/S/E/W\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 2. Panda3DBackend (&#96;gui/renderers/panda3d_backend.py&#96;)\\\\n\\\\nIn-process Panda3D renderer that embeds a Panda3D window in a QWidget and drives it with a &#96;QTimer&#96; calling &#96;taskMgr.step()&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n### BaseBackend implementation\\\\n\\\\n- **&#96;start(parent_widget)&#96;**: Creates &#96;ShowBase&#96; with &#96;window-type none&#96;, embeds into the parent via &#96;winId()&#96;, sets up lighting, input, textures, and a 16 ms &#96;QTimer&#96; for &#96;_step()&#96;. If a snapshot was already received, calls &#96;_rebuild_scene&#96;.\\\\n- **&#96;stop()&#96;**: Stops the timer, closes the graphics window, destroys ShowBase.\\\\n- **&#96;is_ready()&#96;**: Returns &#96;_started and _base is not None&#96;.\\\\n- **&#96;send_maze_update(snapshot_dict)&#96;**: Stores the snapshot and calls &#96;_rebuild_scene&#96; if started.\\\\n- **&#96;send_highlight_player(row, col)&#96;**: Updates &#96;_player_row&#96;/&#96;_player_col&#96;, moves the player node, and updates the minimap.\\\\n- **&#96;send_view_direction(direction)&#96;**: Updates &#96;_facing_h&#96;/&#96;_facing_str&#96;, sets camera heading, and updates the minimap.\\\\n- **&#96;inject_key(panda_key, pressed)&#96;**: Sends &#96;panda_key&#96; or &#96;panda_key-up&#96; via Panda3D messenger.\\\\n\\\\n### 3D scene construction\\\\n\\\\n- **Floor** (&#96;_build_cell_floor&#96;): CardMaker quads at z=0, rotated -90°. Uses fog color for non-visible cells, gate colors for gate cells, procedural floor texture for normal cells.\\\\n- **Ceiling** (&#96;_build_cell_ceiling&#96;): CardMaker quads at z=WALL_HEIGHT (3.0), rotated 90°, procedural ceiling texture.\\\\n- **Walls** (&#96;_build_cell_walls&#96;): CardMaker quads for N/S/E/W edges where there is no connection. Uses &#96;connections&#96; to decide which walls to draw.\\\\n- **Markers** (&#96;_build_cell_markers&#96;): Floating markers for exit (green) and gates (orange/unsolved, green/solved).\\\\n- **Minimap** (&#96;_rebuild_minimap&#96;): 2D overlay in the top-right with colored cells, connections, and a player arrow.\\\\n\\\\nConstants: &#96;CELL_SIZE=4.0&#96;, &#96;WALL_HEIGHT=3.0&#96;, &#96;EYE_HEIGHT=1.6&#96;, &#96;FPS_INTERVAL_MS=16&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n### Input handling\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;_setup_input()&#96;: Registers Panda3D accept handlers for W/S/Q/E/A/D and arrow keys, mapped to &#96;forward&#96;, &#96;backward&#96;, &#96;turn_left&#96;, &#96;turn_right&#96;.\\\\n- &#96;_set_key(action, value)&#96;: Updates &#96;_key_map&#96; and calls &#96;_handle_key_press&#96; on press.\\\\n- &#96;_handle_key_press(action)&#96;: Turn actions update &#96;_facing_h&#96; and emit facing; move actions emit direction via &#96;_emit_direction&#96;/&#96;_emit_facing&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n### Start/stop\\\\n\\\\n- **Start**: Lazy via &#96;start(parent_widget)&#96; when the viewport host is shown. Uses &#96;loadPrcFileData&#96; for &#96;window-type none&#96; and &#96;audio-library-name null&#96;.\\\\n- **Stop**: Called from &#96;MazeCanvas.closeEvent&#96; via &#96;backend.stop()&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 3. MazeCanvas (&#96;gui/maze_canvas.py&#96;)\\\\n\\\\n&#96;MazeCanvas&#96; is a QWidget that can use a pluggable 3D backend and always renders a 2D QPainter minimap.\\\\n\\\\n### Constructor\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\\\ndef __init__(\\\\n    self,\\\\n    parent: QWidget | None = None,\\\\n    *,\\\\n    use_godot: bool = True,\\\\n    godot_parent_widget: QWidget | None = None,\\\\n    backend: BaseBackend | None = None,\\\\n) -&gt; None\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n- If &#96;backend&#96; is provided: uses &#96;_init_backend(backend)&#96;.\\\\n- Else if &#96;use_godot&#96;: tries &#96;_init_godot_backend(godot_parent_widget)&#96;.\\\\n- Else: 2D fallback (&#96;_fallback_reason = \\\\\\\"3D disabled\\\\\\\"&#96;).\\\\n\\\\n### Backend wiring\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;_init_backend(backend)&#96;: Sets &#96;_backend&#96;, &#96;_backend_available=True&#96;, and registers &#96;on_direction&#96; and &#96;on_facing&#96;.\\\\n- &#96;update_maze(snapshot: MazeSnapshot)&#96;: Builds a dict from &#96;snapshot.cells&#96; and calls &#96;backend.send_maze_update({width, height, cells})&#96;.\\\\n- &#96;highlight_player(pos: tuple[int, int])&#96;: Calls &#96;backend.send_highlight_player(pos[0], pos[1])&#96;.\\\\n- &#96;set_view_direction(direction: str)&#96;: Updates &#96;_facing_dir&#96; and calls &#96;backend.send_view_direction(d)&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n### Key forwarding\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;keyPressEvent&#96; / &#96;keyReleaseEvent&#96;: Map Qt keys to Panda3D names via &#96;_QT_KEY_TO_PANDA&#96; and call &#96;backend.inject_key(panda_key, pressed=True/False)&#96; when a backend is available and the event is not auto-repeat.\\\\n\\\\n### Signals\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;direction_clicked(str)&#96; — movement direction\\\\n- &#96;facing_changed(str)&#96; — facing change\\\\n- &#96;godot_process_started(int)&#96; — Godot PID (Godot backend only)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 4. gui_main.py — Panda3D backend management\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;_create_panda3d_canvas()&#96;\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\\\ndef _create_panda3d_canvas(self) -&gt; MazeCanvas:\\\\n    from gui.renderers.panda3d_backend import Panda3DBackend\\\\n    backend = Panda3DBackend()\\\\n    canvas = MazeCanvas(use_godot=False, backend=backend)\\\\n    return canvas\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nCreates a &#96;Panda3DBackend&#96; and a &#96;MazeCanvas&#96; that uses it.\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;_ensure_panda3d_started()&#96;\\\\n\\\\n- Runs only when &#96;renderer == \\\\\\\"panda3d\\\\\\\"&#96; and the canvas has a backend.\\\\n- Calls &#96;backend.start(self._viewport_host)&#96; if not ready.\\\\n- Schedules &#96;_schedule_panda3d_size_sync()&#96; after start.\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;_schedule_panda3d_size_sync(_attempts=0)&#96;\\\\n\\\\n- Polls until the Panda3D window size matches the host widget (with DPR).\\\\n- Uses exponential backoff (50 ms × 2^attempts, max 400 ms) for up to 8 attempts.\\\\n- Stops when sizes match or max attempts reached.\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;showEvent&#96;\\\\n\\\\n- Uses &#96;QTimer.singleShot(0, self._ensure_panda3d_started)&#96; so Panda3D starts after layout has assigned sizes.\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;eventFilter&#96;\\\\n\\\\n- Installed on &#96;_viewport_host&#96;.\\\\n- On &#96;Resize&#96;, &#96;Show&#96;, or &#96;WindowStateChange&#96;:\\\\n  - Godot: &#96;_sync_embedded_godot_viewport()&#96;\\\\n  - Panda3D: &#96;_ensure_panda3d_started()&#96; and &#96;_sync_panda3d_viewport()&#96;\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;_sync_panda3d_viewport()&#96;\\\\n\\\\n- Calls &#96;backend._handle_resize()&#96; if the backend has it.\\\\n\\\\n### Key forwarding\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;keyPressEvent&#96; / &#96;keyReleaseEvent&#96;: When &#96;renderer == \\\\\\\"panda3d\\\\\\\"&#96; and the canvas is a &#96;MazeCanvas&#96;, forwards to &#96;self._canvas.keyPressEvent&#96; / &#96;keyReleaseEvent&#96; and returns; otherwise calls &#96;super()&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 5. &#96;--renderer&#96; flag parsing (&#96;main.py&#96;)\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;StartupConfig&#96; (lines 413–421)\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\\\n@dataclass\\\\nclass StartupConfig:\\\\n    reset_game: bool = False\\\\n    maze_size: int = 3\\\\n    maze_seed: int = 0\\\\n    num_gates: int = 1\\\\n    gui: bool = False\\\\n    use_godot: bool = False\\\\n    renderer: str = \\\\\\\"panda3d\\\\\\\"\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;_parse_startup_flags&#96; (lines 424–458)\\\\n\\\\n- &#96;--renderer &lt;val&gt;&#96;: Requires &#96;val&#96; in &#96;(\\\\\\\"panda3d\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"godot\\\\\\\")&#96;; sets &#96;config.renderer&#96; and &#96;config.use_godot = (val == \\\\\\\"godot\\\\\\\")&#96;.\\\\n- &#96;--no-godot&#96;: Sets &#96;renderer = \\\\\\\"panda3d\\\\\\\"&#96; and &#96;use_godot = False&#96;.\\\\n- Conflict: &#96;--renderer godot&#96; and &#96;--no-godot&#96; together raise &#96;ValueError&#96;.\\\\n- If &#96;explicit_renderer&#96; is set, it overrides; otherwise &#96;--no-godot&#96; forces Panda3D.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 6. Snapshot data structures (&#96;main.py&#96;)\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;CellView&#96; (lines 19–30)\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\\\n@dataclass\\\\nclass CellView:\\\\n    row: int\\\\n    col: int\\\\n    kind: str       # \\\\\\\"start\\\\\\\" | \\\\\\\"exit\\\\\\\" | \\\\\\\"normal\\\\\\\"\\\\n    visible: bool\\\\n    is_player: bool\\\\n    has_gate: bool\\\\n    solved: bool\\\\n    connections: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n### &#96;MazeSnapshot&#96; (lines 33–40)\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\\\n@dataclass\\\\nclass MazeSnapshot:\\\\n    width: int\\\\n    height: int\\\\n    cells: list[CellView] = field(default_factory=list)\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n### Dict format for backends\\\\n\\\\n&#96;MazeCanvas.update_maze&#96; converts &#96;MazeSnapshot&#96; to a plain dict:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\\\n{\\\\n    \\\\\\\"width\\\\\\\": snapshot.width,\\\\n    \\\\\\\"height\\\\\\\": snapshot.height,\\\\n    \\\\\\\"cells\\\\\\\": [\\\\n        {\\\\n            \\\\\\\"row\\\\\\\": cv.row, \\\\\\\"col\\\\\\\": cv.col, \\\\\\\"kind\\\\\\\": cv.kind,\\\\n            \\\\\\\"visible\\\\\\\": cv.visible, \\\\\\\"is_player\\\\\\\": cv.is_player,\\\\n            \\\\\\\"has_gate\\\\\\\": cv.has_gate, \\\\\\\"solved\\\\\\\": cv.solved,\\\\n            \\\\\\\"connections\\\\\\\": list(cv.connections),\\\\n        }\\\\n        for cv in snapshot.cells\\\\n    ]\\\\n}\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n### Production of &#96;MazeSnapshot&#96;\\\\n\\\\n&#96;GameEngine._build_maze_snapshot()&#96; (lines 198–222) iterates over all cells, computes &#96;visible&#96; from &#96;_visited&#96;, &#96;has_gate&#96; / &#96;solved&#96; from &#96;puzzle_id&#96; and &#96;_solved_gates&#96;, and &#96;connections&#96; from &#96;maze.available_moves(p)&#96; for visible cells. The result is attached to Instead of `QtGui.QImage.Format_RGB32`, use `QtGui.QImage.Format.Format_RGB32`.[1]<br/><br/>## Recommended Approach: Convert to QImage<br/><br/>Rather than using SDL_WINDOWID directly (which has been problematic), a more reliable method is converting the pygame surface to a QImage and displaying it in a QWidget:<br/><br/>```python<br/>class ImageWidget(QtGui.QWidget):<br/>    def __init__(self, surface, parent=None):<br/>        super(ImageWidget, self).__init__(parent)<br/>        w = surface.get_width()<br/>        h = surface.get_height()<br/>        self.data = surface.get_buffer().raw<br/>        self.image = QtGui.QImage(self.data, w, h, QtGui.QImage.Format.Format_RGB32)<br/>    <br/>    def paintEvent(self, event):<br/>        qp = QtGui.QPainter()<br/>        qp.begin(self)<br/>        qp.drawImage(0, 0, self.image)<br/>        qp.end()<br/>```<br/><br/>Then embed this widget in your PyQt6 window.[1]<br/><br/>## Known Issues with SDL_WINDOWID<br/><br/>The SDL_WINDOWID approach was broken in Pygame 2 but has been addressed through a pull request implementing `SDL_CreateWindowFrom` in the display module.[3][4] This suggests the feature may work better in more recent pygame versions (2023+). |

All 5 phases are complete. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

**New files created:**
- `gui/renderers/raycaster.py` -- Pure Pygame raycaster module with DDA wall-casting, distance fog, minimap overlay, and grid/angle utilities
- `gui/renderers/pygame_backend.py` -- `PygameBackend` (implements `BaseBackend`) with off-screen rendering, safe `QImage` blitting via `PygameViewport`, DPR-aware sizing, and `QTimer` render loop at ~60fps
- `pygame_standalone_test.py` -- Standalone Pygame window for validating the raycaster with WASD/arrow keys
- `pygame_debug_harness.py` -- PyQt6 debug harness with manual controls and `--sweep-angles` automated test (mirrors `panda3d_debug_harness.py`)
- `tests/test_pygame_backend.py` -- 40 tests covering angle conversions, input handling, callbacks, safe-before-start, orientation correctness (all 8 turn directions), grid building, ray casting, lifecycle, and MazeCanvas integration

**Modified files:**
- `main.py` -- `--renderer pygame` accepted as a valid value; updated CLI usage string
- `gui_main.py` -- Added `_create_pygame_canvas()`, `_ensure_pygame_started()`, `_sync_pygame_viewport()`, pygame branch in `eventFilter`, `showEvent`, and key forwarding
- `tests/test_main_cli_flags.py` -- Added `--renderer pygame` and `--renderer pygame --no-godot` tests; updated invalid-renderer regex
- `tests/test_gui_main_renderer.py` -- Added `test_mainwindow_pygame_viewport_resize_sync`
- `requirements.txt` -- Added `pygame>=2.5`

**Test results:** 204 passed, 0 failed.

You can test with:
- `python pygame_standalone_test.py --size 5 --seed 42` (standalone raycaster window)
- `python pygame_debug_harness.py --sweep-angles --auto-quit-on-sweep-done --size 5 --seed 42` (automated sweep)
- `python main.py --gui --renderer pygame` (full game integration)
